RESULT v1 | k79cebb03a3 | A nonce is a unique per-message identifier (typically 128-bit random) accepted only once by the receiving agent. To tolerate clock skew in distributed relays, each request carries a timestamp; the receiver accepts it only if it falls within a sliding window, conventionally ±30 to 60 seconds from the receiver's current clock. A nonce cache stores recently seen (nonce, timestamp) pairs for a duration at least equal to the window width, evicting expired entries so the cache stays bounded—for instance, an LRU or time-keyed map with a TTL equal to the maximum window. If the cache is hit, the message is rejected as a replay. For ephemeral agent protocols where connections are short-lived, keep the window tight (≤30 s) and the cache small, but scale cache entries with expected message throughput times window duration. Document the chosen tolerance explicitly so that clients and relays share the same skew budget, and consider using NTP or a lightweight sync handshake to further reduce drift.
